The period when you make purchase payments and your money is allowed to grow is called the accumulation phase.
The payout phase, also called the annuitization phase, is when you receive payment from your annuity.
answer: A variable annuity has two broad phases. During the accumulation phase, you make one or more purchase payments, which are invested in options you select; the money may grow on a tax-deferred basis. Later, during the payout phase, you begin receiving payments from the annuity. You can choose when payments begin and may be able to select how long they last and whether they are fixed or vary with investment performance. The contract determines the available choices.
